name: Work Permit

requirements.blocker_text: A person not belonging to Montserrat may not engage in any occupation for profit or reward, or take employment for wage, salary, or other remuneration, without a valid work permit (Immigration Act, Section 21).
Application is submitted to the Governor in Council; approval or denial is discretionary. Approved permits require the employer to file an annual report (Form 'O') between 1-15 January.

evidence_required.document: Work permit application to the Governor in Council
Employer's annual report (Form 'O'), filed 1-15 January each year of the permit's validity

outcome.duration_length: not specified in the Immigration Act text reviewed

sources.title: Montserrat Chapter 13.01, Immigration Act -- Section 21 (work permits: prohibition on unauthorised employment for non-belongers, application to Governor in Council, employer annual reporting, penalties), Section 22 (exemptions)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Montserrat's initial build, sourced directly from primary legislation. Section 21 also criminalises unauthorised employment (fine up to $1,000 or 6 months' imprisonment, plus $100/day for a continuing offence) and Section 22 exempts categories such as High Court judges, government employees, diplomatic representatives, and certain international-organisation staff -- these exemptions are not modelled as their own route since they are narrow carve-outs, not a general immigration pathway. Permit duration, specific document/fee requirements, and category distinctions (e.g. skilled vs unskilled) are not detailed in the Act text itself -- these likely live in subsidiary Work Permit Regulations that were not located at tier-1 in this pass; flagged as a gap rather than guessed. renewable is set true based on the existence of annual employer reporting obligations implying an ongoing/renewing permit, not a confirmed fixed term.
